content: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir inhibits the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4, leading to increased levels or effects of various drugs metabolized by this pathway. Below are the detailed interactions and clinical recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Methylprednisolone: Co-administration with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir can increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. Monitor closely. 2. Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases exposure to unconjugated DM4, the cytotoxic component of this antibody-drug conjugate, potentially increasing adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 3. Mometasone (Inhaled): Co-administration may elevate systemic corticosteroid levels, increasing the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids and monitor closely. 4. Nelfinavir: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nelfinavir levels. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events. 5. Nevirapine: Co-administration increases nevirapine levels. Use caution and monitor. 6. Nicardipine: Increased levels may lead to side effects like hypotension, flushing, and edema. Consider temporary dose reduction and monitor closely. 7. Nifedipine: Co-administration may require a 50% dose reduction during and for three days after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. Monitor closely. 8. Norgestrel: Increased systemic concentrations may heighten the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 9. Oxycodone: Elevated levels may increase the risk of respiratory depression. Monitor therapeutic and adverse effects closely, and reduce the dose if necessary. 10. Prednisone: Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid levels, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. Monitor closely. 11. Quetiapine: Reduce the dose to one-sixth when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 12. Quizartinib: Reduce the dose to 4 mg/day when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for five half-lives. 13. Raltgravir: Ritonavir induces UGT1A1, potentially decreasing raltegravir levels. Use caution and monitor. 14. Rifabutin: Co-administration increases rifabutin levels, potentially causing neutropenia and uveitis. Reduce the rifabutin dose by at least 75% to 150 mg every other day or three times weekly. Monitor closely. 15. Riociguat: Increased levels may cause hypotension. Consider temporary dose reduction and monitor for signs of hypotension. 16. Rosuvastatin: Nirmatrelvir inhibits OATP1B1, increasing rosuvastatin levels. Consider temporary discontinuation during treatment. 17. Seladelpar: Use caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 18. Tenofovir AF: Co-administration may increase systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 19. Tipranavir: Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated. Monitor for increased adverse events. 20. Trazodone: Co-administration may cause nausea, dizziness, hypotension, and syncope. Consider lowering the trazodone dose. 21. Triamcinolone (Injectable Suspension): Increased systemic corticosteroid levels may raise the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. Monitor closely. 22. Triamcinolone (Inhaled): Similar to the injectable form, co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid levels. Consider alternatives and monitor. 23. Vamorolone: Reduce the starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. Monitor closely. 24. Vardenafil: Co-administration increases levels. Limit the dose to 5 mg every 72 hours. 25. Venlafaxine: Increased levels may heighten toxicity. Use caution and monitor. 26. Verapamil: Increased levels may cause bradycardia, hypotension, or dizziness. Temporarily pause the antihypertensive drug if needed. 27. Vinblastine: Co-administration may lead to significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. Use caution and monitor. 28. Vincristine: Similar to vinblastine, co-administration may cause significant hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. Use caution and monitor. 29. Voxilaprevir: Co-administration increases levels. Use caution and monitor. 30. Warfarin: INR may increase or decrease. Monitor INR closely during co-administration. 31. Zanubrutinib: Reduce the dose to 80 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 32. Zidovudine: Co-administration decreases levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 33. Zuranolone: Reduce the dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 34. Emtricitabine: Minor interaction with unknown significance. Monitor closely. 35. Irbesartan: Co-administration may decrease levels due to weak CYP2C9 induction by ritonavir. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of treatment. 36. Losartan: Co-administration may increase conversion to its active metabolite. Monitor closely. 37. Macitentan: Co-administration has a low expected interaction magnitude. No dosage adjustment is required. 38. Mycophenolate: Co-administration may alter levels due to glucuronidation. Monitor closely. 39. Sacubitril/Valsartan: Co-administration may increase levels due to inhibition of hepatic uptake transporters. No dosage modification is needed. 40. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Co-administration may decrease levels through CYP2B6 metabolism. Monitor closely. 41. Valsartan: Co-administration may increase levels due to inhibition of hepatic uptake transporters. No dosage modification is needed. 42. Abemaciclib: Reduce the dose when co-administered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely. 43. Adagrasib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until steady-state concentrations are reached (~8 days). Use alternative drugs if necessary. 44. Alfuzosin: Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. 45. Aliskiren: Avoid co-administration with CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors. Use alternative drugs. 46. Alprazolam: Consider lowering the dose when co-administered with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. Monitor closely. 47. Amiodarone: Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening reactions. 48. Amlodipine: Reduce the dose by 50% during and for three days after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. Monitor closely. 49. Apalutamide: Co-administration is contraindicated as it decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels significantly. Avoid use.
